beats.title: Sargon Founds the Akkadian Empire
beats.description: A Mesopotamian ruler of humble origins united the city-states of Sumer and Akkad, creating the first empire in history.
beats.note: Conventional middle-chronology date for his rise.

beats.title: Hammurabi Begins Babylon's Rise
beats.description: Hammurabi took the throne of a modest city on the Euphrates and began conquests that built a great Mesopotamian realm.

beats.title: Ahmose Founds Egypt's New Kingdom
beats.description: A Theban prince drove the Hyksos rulers out of the Nile delta and reunited Egypt, opening its age of conquest abroad.

beats.title: Neo-Assyrian Empire Rises
beats.description: Assyrian kings began a campaign of reconquest that grew into a vast and feared military empire across the Near East.
beats.note: Start of Adad-nirari II's reign, the conventional start.

beats.title: Nabopolassar Founds Neo-Babylonia
beats.description: A Chaldean leader seized Babylon from Assyrian control and founded the dynasty that would rebuild the city in splendour.

beats.title: Cyrus Founds the Persian Empire
beats.description: Cyrus overthrew the Median king and merged Persians and Medes into the largest empire the world had yet seen.

beats.title: Athens Forms the Delian League
beats.description: Greek city-states pooled ships and money against Persia under Athenian leadership, a league that became an Athenian empire.

beats.title: Alexander Invades Persia
beats.description: A young Macedonian king crossed the Hellespont with his army, beginning conquests that reached from Greece to India.
beats.why_in: founder's first conquest of Alexander's empire

beats.title: Chandragupta Founds Maurya Empire
beats.description: An Indian adventurer overthrew the Nanda dynasty and began uniting the subcontinent into its first great empire.
beats.note: Dates vary by a few years; 322 BC is the common one.

beats.title: Arsaces Founds the Parthian Empire
beats.description: A nomad chieftain seized a province from the Seleucid kings, starting the dynasty that later rivalled Rome in the East.

beats.title: Qin Unifies China
beats.description: The king of Qin conquered the last rival state and took the title of First Emperor over a single united China.

beats.title: Modu Builds the Xiongnu Empire
beats.description: A steppe prince killed his own father and seized the leadership, forging the nomad tribes into a power that menaced China.
beats.why_in: founding of the Xiongnu steppe empire

beats.title: Liu Bang Founds the Han Dynasty
beats.description: A peasant-born rebel defeated his rival and became emperor, founding a dynasty that ruled China for four centuries.

beats.title: The Roman Empire Begins
beats.description: The Senate granted Octavian a new title and powers, ending the Republic and making him the first Roman emperor.

beats.title: Ardashir Founds the Sasanian Empire
beats.description: A Persian ruler defeated the last Parthian king in battle and restored a native Iranian empire that rivalled Rome and Byzantium.

beats.title: Chandragupta I Founds Gupta Empire
beats.description: A king of Magadha began the dynasty whose realm would be remembered as a golden age of Indian science and art.

beats.title: The Umayyad Caliphate Begins
beats.description: Mu'awiya became sole ruler of the Muslim world and made Damascus the capital of a hereditary caliphate.

beats.title: The Abbasid Caliphate Takes Power
beats.description: A revolt from the east overthrew the ruling caliphs and placed a new dynasty on the throne, soon ruling from Baghdad.

beats.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
beats.description: The pope placed a crown on the Frankish king on Christmas Day, reviving an emperor in western Europe.

beats.title: Jayavarman II Launches Khmer Empire
beats.description: A Cambodian prince declared himself universal monarch in a ritual on a sacred hill, beginning the empire of Angkor.

beats.title: Otto I Crowned Holy Roman Emperor
beats.description: A German king was crowned in Rome by the pope, founding the empire that would last in Central Europe for centuries.
beats.why_in: founding of the Holy Roman Empire

beats.title: Seljuks Seize Nishapur
beats.description: Turkic chieftain Tughril took a great Persian city from the Ghaznavids, the first step in founding the Seljuk Empire.
beats.why_in: founder's first conquest of the Seljuk Empire

beats.title: Genghis Khan Founds Mongol Empire
beats.description: A great assembly of steppe tribes proclaimed Temujin as universal ruler, launching history's largest land empire.

beats.title: Sundiata Founds the Mali Empire
beats.description: A West African prince defeated the sorcerer-king of the Sosso at Kirina and built a rich empire on the gold trade.

beats.title: Solomonic Dynasty Rules Ethiopia
beats.description: A highland noble overthrew the previous dynasty and claimed descent from Solomon, beginning the long Ethiopian imperial line.

beats.title: Osman Founds the Ottoman State
beats.description: A Turkish frontier chieftain in Anatolia declared his independence, starting the dynasty that would conquer Constantinople.
beats.note: Traditional date; sources vary by a few years.

beats.title: Vijayanagara Empire Is Founded
beats.description: Two brothers in southern India founded a Hindu kingdom that grew into a great empire and a wealthy capital city.

beats.title: Timur Founds the Timurid Empire
beats.description: A Turco-Mongol warlord took power in Samarkand and set out on conquests that reached from Delhi to Damascus.

beats.title: Portugal Captures Ceuta
beats.description: A Portuguese fleet seized a rich Moroccan port, the first overseas conquest of Europe's first global colonial empire.

beats.title: The Aztec Triple Alliance
beats.description: Three cities of the Valley of Mexico joined forces against their rival, laying the foundation of the Aztec empire.

beats.title: Pachacuti Builds the Inca Empire
beats.description: After repelling an attack on Cusco, a young Inca ruler began transforming a small highland kingdom into a vast Andean empire.

beats.title: Sunni Ali Takes Timbuktu
beats.description: The Songhai king captured the great desert trading city, the key conquest in building a new West African empire.
beats.why_in: founder's first conquest of the Songhai Empire

beats.title: Ismail I Founds Safavid Persia
beats.description: A teenage Sufi leader took Tabriz and crowned himself shah, restoring a unified Iranian state with Shia Islam as its faith.

beats.title: Cortes Lands in Mexico
beats.description: A Spanish adventurer burned his ships on the Gulf coast and marched inland, beginning the conquest that built an empire in the Americas.
beats.why_in: founder's first conquest of Spain's American empire

beats.title: Babur Wins at Panipat
beats.description: A Central Asian prince used gunpowder weapons to defeat the Sultan of Delhi, establishing the Mughal Empire in India.

beats.title: England Founds Jamestown
beats.description: English colonists built a fort on the Virginia coast, the first lasting settlement in what became the British Empire.
beats.why_in: first permanent colony of the British Empire
beats.note: Chosen over the East India Company charter; both are defensible.

beats.title: Peter the Great Becomes Emperor
beats.description: After victory over Sweden, the Russian tsar took the title of emperor, proclaiming his country a European empire.

beats.title: Napoleon Crowns Himself Emperor
beats.description: In Notre-Dame cathedral, the French general took the crown from the pope's hands and placed it on his own head.

beats.title: Shaka Founds the Zulu Kingdom
beats.description: A chief of a small clan in southern Africa reorganised his army and began conquests that forged a powerful Zulu state.

beats.title: Meiji Restoration Begins
beats.description: Rebels overthrew the shogun and restored the emperor to power, launching Japan's rapid rise as a modern empire.
beats.why_in: founding of the Empire of Japan

beats.title: German Empire Is Proclaimed
beats.description: German princes gathered in the Hall of Mirrors of a defeated enemy's palace to crown the Prussian king as emperor.
